Name: Acidic Flask
Notes: 5 + [Clubs] stacks of Bleeding on hit. Suit-scaling added: a bare flip has exactly a 1-in-4 chance of matching a specific suit (1 card in the suit pool for an unmodified flip), so the marginal 6th-stack value (11.75-11.5=0.25) is credited at x0.25 -- 0.25 x 0.5(on-hit) x 0.25(suit) = 0.03125. Bleeding's Clubs pairing is the established convention (RULES_DESIGN.md's Suit portfolio table, also matching Reckoning/Beast Venom's real [Clubs] Crippled text). Barely moves the needle since Bleeding is already near its ~12 asymptotic cap at 5 stacks. Value 1.28125, Net -1.71875, still an accepted below-budget utility item per the designer's earlier call.

Name: Immaculate Adhesive
Notes: 2 levels of Difficult Terrain in the target space and all adjacent spaces, lasting the encounter. Recomputed under the newly re-derived, non-linear Difficult Terrain curve (see design/balance_weights_notes.md) rather than the old flat 0.55/degree rate: 2 degrees hits the curve's hard cap at 8.25 (Agility-3/Speed-4 baseline). Guaranteed (no attack roll -- the effect auto-succeeds), so no hit-chance discount, but the flat Autoswing (5.5) opportunity-cost subtraction still applies same as every other Grenade. Priced for 1 creature actually crossing the full 2 degrees (the primary target, per the designer's own call -- only the one directly hit needs to cross the terrain at all), plus a half-credit margin (half of 1 degree's own value, 1.375) for the incidental area-denial value of a second creature losing an AP or so trying to cross it, or others taking suboptimal repositioning -- not a full second creature, since most of the party will just walk around the zone rather than commit to crossing it. Value 4.125, Net +1.125 -- deliberately a bit above the Level-1 threshold (0.8), since a genuine chokepoint should reward smart tactical placement rather than sitting exactly at budget. Net moves from the old flat-rate model's -6.3 to +1.125, resolving the structural ceiling problem flagged earlier in this pass.

Name: Bottled Fire
Notes: 8 Fire damage on hit (bumped from 7). Recomputed under the unified Grenade model: margin (8-3)x2=10, plus the +1 universal Harried credit any attack vs. Dodge/Parry grants, minus Autoswing (5.5) as the flat opportunity cost of not just attacking instead. Net moves to -0.5, within the Level-2 threshold (0.975) -- matches the same 1-damage-point bump the designer worked out by hand earlier in this pass, before applying it to the ledger.

Name: Smokejar
Notes: 3 + [Clubs] Crippled + a growing smoke/Heavy Cover zone for the scene. Suit-scaling added: marginal 4th-stack Crippled value (15-9=6) x 0.5(on-hit) x 0.25(suit) = +0.75. Clubs is the established Crippled convention (RULES_DESIGN.md's Suit portfolio table, matching Reckoning/Beast Venom's real [Clubs] Crippled text). Value 6.25, Net +0.25, within the Level-2 threshold (0.975). (Difficult Terrain deliberately NOT suit-scaled here -- that was briefly considered for Immaculate Adhesive instead, a mix-up caught and corrected; Smokejar was always the Crippled-suit-scaling target.)

Name: Bonemelter
Notes: 3 + [Diamonds] stacks of Necrotic + 8 Shadow damage on hit. Suit-scaling added: Necrotic's marginal stack is linear (no stacking curve/cap the way Bleeding/Crippled/Vulnerable have), so the addition lands at full weight: 1.5 x 0.25(suit) = +0.375 (Necrotic's own situational-realization discount is already baked into its 1.5/stack rate, not reapplied). Diamonds is the established Necrotic convention (RULES_DESIGN.md's Suit portfolio table). Value 10.375, Net +1.375 -- a small overshoot past the Level-3 threshold (1.15), accepted as-is per the designer.

Name: Snowstorm
Notes: 8 Frost damage + Slowed 3 + [Spades] times on hit. Suit-scaling added: marginal 4th-stack Slowed value (11-6.6=4.4) x 0.5(on-hit) x 0.25(suit) = +0.55. Spades is the established Slowed convention (RULES_DESIGN.md's Suit portfolio table, matching Spectral Spiderwebs/Beast Venom's real [Spades] Slowed text). Value 9.35, Net +0.35, still within the Level-3 threshold (1.15).

Name: Sunbeam
Notes: 9 Brilliant damage + Vulnerable 4 + [Diamonds] stacks on hit. Suit-scaling added: marginal 5th-stack Vulnerable value (14-10=4) x 0.5(on-hit) x 0.25(suit) = +0.5. Diamonds is the established Vulnerable convention (RULES_DESIGN.md's Suit portfolio table). Value 13.0, Net +1.0, within the Level-4 threshold (1.325).

Name: Hellfire Bomb
Notes: 8 Fire damage, hitting all creatures adjacent to the target (AoE, 2-enemy assumption). Recomputed with the AoE realization discount: (DamageComponent 20 + Harried 2) x0.8(realization) = 17.6, -5.5 Autoswing (undiscounted) = Value 12.1, Net +0.1 -- within the Level-4 threshold (1.325), resolving the overshoot flagged earlier this pass without touching raw Damage at all. See design/balance_weights_notes.md's AoE multiplier section for the full derivation (net 1.6x = 2x enemies-hit assumption x 0.8 realization).

Name: Thunderclap-in-a-Jar
Grants: Damage:16(post-AoE), Bleeding:2+[Clubs] per-target(AoE-multiplied, corrected), Harried:2+[Diamonds] per-target(AoE-multiplied)+2(universal, AoE-doubled)
Notes: 8 Physical damage + 2+[Clubs] Bleeding + 2+[Diamonds] Harried per-target, area-targeted (AoE, 2-enemy assumption). Recomputed under the corrected AoE-curve method (curve(N) x2, not curve(2N) -- see design/balance_weights_notes.md's AoE multiplier correction): per-target Bleeding(2)=8 + suit-scaled expected marginal (0.25 x (Bleeding(3)-Bleeding(2))=0.5) = 8.5, x0.5(on-hit)=4.25, x2(AoE, independent targets)=8.5. Per-target Harried-bonus(2)=2 + suit-scaled expected marginal (0.25x1=0.25)=2.25, x0.5=1.125, x2=2.25 -- unaffected by the correction since Harried is linear below its cap either way. Damage margin (8-4)x2=8 (per-target, linear, unaffected) x2(AoE)=16. + Harried universal (2, AoE-doubled) = total pre-realization 16+8.5+2.25+2=28.75, x0.8(realization)=23.0, -5.5 Autoswing = Value 17.5, Net +2.5. Lower than the previous (bugged) computation's +5.34 -- Bleeding's tapering curve was actually being under-credited by the old curve(2N) method, but the Damage margin (the larger component) is unaffected since it's linear, so the net change is still a real decrease. Still overshooting the Level-5 threshold (1.5) by a real amount, not just a rounding edge -- flagged for a follow-up decision (trim the Bleeding/Harried-bonus stacks, or accept as an intentionally-strong signature item), not resolved here.

Name: Reeler
Notes: Renamed from Quartz Tincture -- redesigned around a concussive, Harried-forward identity per the designer's call (a gap worth having in the Grenade lineup). 8 Fire damage (matching the L2-L3 sibling baseline) + 4 + [Diamonds] stacks of Harried on hit. Since Harried's own curve caps hard at 6 stacks (value 6 guaranteed / 3 discounted -- see design/balance_weights_notes.md), it can never carry much budget alone; going with Option B (genuine suit-scaling, base 4 usually landing 4-5, rarely 6) over flatly maxing it at 6 (which would make suit-scaling contribute nothing and read as misleading flavor text) or bumping raw damage to 9 (which would tie Sunbeam's Level 4 number). Value: margin (8-3)x2=10, Harried(4)=4x0.5=2, marginal 5th-stack suit credit (5-4)x0.5x0.25=0.125, +1 universal Harried, -5.5 Autoswing = 7.625. Net -1.375 -- an accepted below-full-budget item, same shape as Acidic Flask/Bottled Fire's earlier near-misses, prioritizing identity over hitting exact budget.

Name: Energizing Brew
Notes: Good Luck on Reflex (initiative), now until a full night's rest instead of 1 hour -- removes the guesswork of timing the drink to a specific fight without stacking extra value, since Reflex is still flipped exactly once per encounter no matter how long the buff is active (designer's explicit call, not re-priced upward for the wider window). Dropped AP:-2 entirely: same 'drunk ahead of time' reasoning as the prevention trio -- you'd have this active before initiative is even rolled, so it never actually competes with an in-combat action. Good Luck's own weight revised this session from 2.2 to 2.4 (see the Good Luck suit-pool correction in design/balance_weights_notes.md) -- GoodLuck(1)=2.4, Net = 2.4-3 = -0.6, clean fit at the Level-1 threshold (0.8).

Name: Fortifying Concoction
Notes: Grants 3 stacks of Protected (reduced from 4) -- never recomputed this session against Protected's own confirmed Locked value (3/stack, guaranteed), which left it badly overpowered at the old 4-stack grant: Value 12, Net +3.5 against a Level-1 budget, more than 4x over. Kept the standard full AP charge rather than the half-AP mixed-use treatment -- per the designer, Protected decays every round it's up, which makes it an inherently in-combat effect (unlike Healing Potion's genuinely split downtime/reactive use), so it doesn't get the same discount. Protected(3)=9, -5.5 AP = Value 3.5, Net +0.5 -- clean fit at the Level-1 threshold (0.8).

Name: Elemental-Attuned Tincture
Notes: Reworked around a redesigned universal Ward: +2 Resist while any stacks remain PLUS each stack can absorb 1 Health loss from that damage type (Protected's mandatory-substitution rule). Grants 3 stacks; these don't decay per-turn (alchemy convention, mirroring Poison), so the flat Resist piece prices at its full undiscounted rate (2.0 Fire, doubled per the Resist correction -- see balance_weights_notes.md). Absorption reuses Protected's own 3/stack rate scaled by the damage-share fraction (2/3): 2.0/stack, unaffected by the Resist fix. Fire: 2.0 + 3x2.0 = 8.0, Net = 8.0-6 = 2.0. Frost/Brilliant/Shadow: 1.0+6.0=7.0, Net=1.0 -- the absorption component still narrows Fire's usual edge.

Name: Essential Ointment
Notes: Draw 2 cards (bumped from 1) -- full AP structurally can't work for a card-draw item at this budget (the flat 5.5 AP tax alone eats most of a Level-2 target), so this moves to the zero-AP treatment instead: drawn cards sit in your hand until your next full night's rest regardless (per the Hand rules), so 'drink it before the scene' is the natural reading, same durability window the zero-AP convention already relies on for the prevention trio/Energizing Brew. Card:2 x 2.7 = 5.4, Net = 5.4-6 = -0.6, clean fit at the Level-2 threshold (0.975) without needing to touch Card's own value.

Name: Soldier's Salts
Notes: Regain the use of any Encounter Technique Level 2 or lower. THE TABEL has no 'refund an ability use' mechanic, so I used a trick: a refunded Technique use is worth that Technique's own Target budget (Level x 3). On its own that pins Value to exactly equal Target, giving zero margin to ever clear the item's own AP cost -- true of every refund-trick item, and why this whole family read badly at first. Fixed with a x1.5 premium on the refund's own baseline (same 'flexibility is worth something extra' reasoning Card's premium over Good Luck already uses), reused for Fighter's Friend/Battlemaster's Brew/Soul Soup below. Re-Leveled from 2 to 1 alongside the premium -- the item wasn't underpowered for what it does, it was costed one Level too high: at Level 1, refunding a Level-2 Technique, the fixed AP tax (a constant 5.5) finally stops eating more of the budget than the premium adds back. 1.5 x (2x3) - 5.5 = 3.5. Net moves from -5.5 to +0.5.

Name: Calming Brew
Notes: Prevents the next 4 total stacks of Taunted/Frightened this encounter (and removes existing stacks up to that total). Rebalanced to be drunk ahead of time -- AP charge dropped entirely (see balance.md): AP only matters in combat, and a 1-hour/pre-fight consumable spent outside initiative was never really competing with an attack. The reactive/emergency case (drinking it mid-fight) isn't separately modeled -- its cost is already implicit in the AP that use actually spends. Moved back to Level 3 (its original placement) rather than staying at Level 2, since 4x2.2=8.8 fits a Level-3 budget cleanly without changing the grant: Net -0.2, within threshold (1.15).

Name: Healing Potion
Notes: Heals 2 Health (Shallow, guaranteed) -- reverted back down from the earlier 3, replacing that bump with a half-AP charge instead. Per the designer: a lot of real use of the system's standard healing item is topping off Health outside of combat, where AP doesn't even exist as a resource -- but it's also genuinely used reactively mid-fight, unlike the L3 prevention trio which is overwhelmingly pre-fight prep. Charged at half the standard AP cost (2.75, 1 AP's value, instead of the full 5.5) to split the difference between those two use cases rather than assume either extreme. ShallowHeal(2)=8, -2.75 = Value 5.25, Net -0.75 -- clean fit at the Level-2 threshold (0.975). See balance.md for the new 'half AP for genuinely mixed-use items' convention this establishes, alongside the existing full-AP (always reactive) and zero-AP (always prep) treatments.

Name: Liquid Charisma
Notes: Good Luck on Presence/Persuasion/Rapport for 1 hour. Dropped AP:-2 entirely -- Social Contests don't spend AP as a resource at all (confirmed earlier this project), so charging AP for a purely social-flip buff was never actually correct. Replaced the old '~2 uses' guess with a real cadence estimate: a Social Contest resolves via a GM-set number of successes earned through Statement flips (Presence/Persuasion/Rapport), and the drinker, as the party's social lead, would typically carry most of the Statements in a scene running up to the full hour -- estimated at ~4 relevant flips, comparable in scope to a moderate combat encounter. Good Luck's own weight revised this session from 2.2 to 2.4 (suit-pool correction, see design/balance_weights_notes.md): GoodLuck(4) = 4 x 2.4 = 9.6, Net = 9.6-9 = 0.6, clean fit at the Level-3 threshold (1.15). Target = Level x 3 was calibrated against combat encounters, so this Net should still be read with that imperfect-fit caveat noted previously.

Name: Earthen Draught
Notes: Tops up to 2 Protected at the end of every turn for 1 hour. Since Protected doesn't stack past the current top-up, most of the ongoing value only matters if it's actually being spent down by incoming hits -- estimated as roughly 3 'refresh' instances worth of value over a 5-round fight (3 x 2 stacks = 6), not 5 refreshes, since some rounds won't need it topped up. Protected's own weight (3/stack) is unchanged this pass, just newly confirmed rather than asserted -- unchanged from the prior recompute.

Name: Fighter's Friend
Notes: Regain use of any Encounter Technique Level 3 or lower -- same refund-trick as Soldier's Salts, now with the x1.5 premium: 1.5 x (3x3) - 5.5 = 8. Re-Leveled from 4 to 3 as part of a reshuffled three-item family (Soldier's Salts now Level 1/refund-2, Fighter's Friend Level 3/refund-3, new Battlemaster's Brew below fills the vacated Level 4/refund-4 slot). Net moves from -5.5 to -1 -- a small, accepted gap, same tier as several other items this session.

Name: Swiftblade Vial
Notes: Redesigned to drop Good Luck entirely, per the designer's call to separate this from Fatebinder's Cordial's identity and lean into a purely speed/tempo theme instead. First explored a direct Extra Success grant, rejected on a new standing rule (design/RULES_DESIGN.md) -- damage/success bonuses stay routed through Good Luck/Defense-reduction/Gambling/suit-pool assists, never granted flat. Landed on turn-order adjustment instead, a mechanic the designer wants to use more broadly and which had no existing value in this model -- first derivation this session, Pencil 1.0/place (see balance_weights_notes.md). Hasted(8) = 0.55x(4x8-6) = 14.3, + TurnOrder(3) = 3.0, = 17.3, -5.5 AP = Value 11.8, Net = 11.8-12 = -0.2, clean fit at the Level-4 threshold (1.325). An earlier draft tried carrying more of the budget through turn-order alone (~9 places against a modest Hasted count) -- far past any existing precedent's scale, which is what pushed this final split toward a smaller, still-untested shift paired with a bigger Hasted component instead.

Name: Battlemaster's Brew
Notes: New item, filling the Level 4 slot vacated when Fighter's Friend re-Leveled down to 3. Regain the use of any Encounter Technique Level 4 or lower -- same refund-trick and x1.5 premium as its siblings: 1.5 x (4x3) - 5.5 = 12.5. Net lands at +0.5, completing the family: Soldier's Salts (L1, refund-2, +0.5), Fighter's Friend (L3, refund-3, -1), Battlemaster's Brew (L4, refund-4, +0.5).

Name: Insanity Potion
Notes: Full rework this pass, replacing the old 'treat any card as a Heart' clause (a leftover from a previous rules version meant to guarantee a damage bonus, no longer needed now that Extra Successes route through Good Luck/suit matching/Gambling) with a Battle Maneuver Battering-style effect: if your attack hits or is Parried, the target gains a stack of Bleeding, running for the whole hour rather than a single proc. Speed(1, non-decaying for the whole encounter) = 0.55 x 4 turns = 2.2 (corrected from the old flat 0.55, which only priced the first-turn marginal). Crippled/Slowed immunity priced as an average, not a sum, of Crippled(3)=9 and Slowed(2)=3.3 -- a fight realistically throws one debuff type at a target, not both at once (same logic Predator's Cry's own Crippled-or-Slowed clause uses) -- average = 6.15. Wounded immunity triangulated two ways (flip-based: ~2 turns x 1 attack+1 defense flip x Bad Luck's 2.2 = 8.8; opportunity-cost: saving the party Healer 2 AP = 5.5; averaged = 7.15) but then assumed, per the designer, to roughly offset the item's own drawback (cannot heal or gain Protected for the hour) rather than pricing both independently -- the drawback exists specifically as a countermeasure to this one piece, so netting them to 0 is more faithful to the original intent than deriving both separately and hoping they happen to cancel. Sustained Bleeding-on-hit priced at Bleeding's own hard cap (12), not a per-proc multiply, since stacks reapplied throughout a whole encounter against one focused target accumulate faster than the 1/turn decay unwinds them. Total = 2.2+6.15+12.0 = 20.35, -5.5 AP = Value 14.85, Net = 14.85-15 = -0.15 -- landing close to neutral by design: per the designer, a capstone item is meant to be a little swingy (stronger in some contexts, offset by its own real drawback in others), with the 'reward cleverness and risk over raw power' principle (see RULES_DESIGN.md) doing more of the work than an inflated Net would.

Name: Kiss of the Earth
Notes: Prevents the next 3 stacks of Bleeding, 1 hour (reduced from 4, and now also removes existing stacks up to that total -- matches Calming Brew's existing wording). Rebalanced to be drunk ahead of time -- AP charge dropped entirely (see balance.md), same reasoning as Calming Brew. Bleeding(3)=10 fits a Level-3 budget cleanly (moved up from Level 2): Net +1.0, within threshold (1.15).

Name: Predator's Cry
Notes: Prevents the next 3 stacks of Crippled or Slowed, until next rest (reduced from 4, moved Level 4->3 to consolidate all three stack-prevention Potions -- Calming Brew, Kiss of the Earth, this one -- into a single Level-3 'preparation item' cluster per the designer's healing-family framework). avg(Crippled(3)=9, Slowed(3)=6.6)=7.8, no AP (drunk ahead of time). Net -1.2, just outside the Level-3 threshold (1.15) by a negligible margin -- accepted as-is.

Name: Revivification Draught
Grants: DeepHeal:4(ticks, player choice of Shallow or Deep), AP:-2
Notes: Reworked from a Level 5 burst-heal (5 immediately + 1/turn for 4 rounds) into a Level 4 pure trickle: 1 Health, player's choice of Shallow or Deep, at the start of each of the next 4 turns. Frees up Level 5 for a different capstone item and gives the healing-Potion family a dedicated 'prevent Wounded over time' option per the designer's framework (L1 Fortifying Concoction/Protected, L2 Healing Potion, L3 stack-prevention cluster, L4 this). Priced at Deep Heal's own rate (5/point) since the Shallow-or-Deep choice belongs to the player, not chance or an enemy -- same 'price the rational best choice' logic as any other player-controlled option, not averaged the way Crippled-or-Slowed was (that choice belongs to the enemy). 4 x 5 = 20, -5.5 AP (kept standard -- explicitly meant to work mid-combat, not just downtime prep, so it doesn't get the 'drunk ahead of time' AP exemption the L3 prevention cluster gets) = Value 14.5, Net +2.5. A deliberate overshoot past the Level-4 threshold (1.325), accepted per the designer given healing's own pricing tension: reactive timing flexibility (apply after you already know the damage landed, no need to predict an incoming hit) versus the rigidity of a fixed per-turn trickle when a player actually needs a lot of healing right now.

Name: Basic Poison
Notes: Structural/carrier item only -- sets Concentration (3+Level) and Potency (=Level) for whichever of the 7 flavors below is chosen; has no standalone mechanical grant of its own, so no Value/Net computed for this row specifically. See I050-I056 for the actual priced flavors, each shown combined with a representative Level-3 Basic Poison (Potency 3).

Name: Crippling Poison
Notes: Representative Level 3 (Potency 3): 3 stacks Crippled on a successful poison-attack. AP cost and the redundant 'poison-landing' discount both DROPPED this session -- see design/balance.md's Poison entry. Per the designer, every Poison effect except Bleeding persists ~1 hour per stack rather than decaying via the normal 1/turn Fleeting rule -- so Crippled's own compounding curve (which assumes decay across its 2-turn survival window) needs its stack count held at FULL strength across both turns instead of tapering: 1.5 x 3 x 2 = 9, not the decaying-curve's 7.5. Net lands at exactly 0 -- no adjustment needed, this item is naturally balanced once every correction is applied. Its 1x-Potency stack grant (vs. Bloody/Necrotic Poison's 2x) turns out to be the right baseline multiplier for a keyword at Crippled's rate.

Name: Bloody Poison
Notes: Representative Level 3: 6 stacks Bleeding (twice Potency) via weapon application -- the ingested version (4x Potency) isn't modeled here since that requires a completely different delivery method, out of scope for a weapon-poison assumption. Bleeding's own curve caps hard at high stack counts (6 stacks = 11.75). AP cost and the redundant 'poison-landing' discount both DROPPED, same as the rest of the batch. Unlike every other Poison, Bleeding is the one explicitly called out as expiring NORMALLY (standard 1/turn Fleeting decay, not the ~1 hour/stack persistence the rest of this batch gets) -- so its curve doesn't get the same full-strength-across-2-turns adjustment Crippling/Slowing/Vulnerability/Harrying Poison do below. REVIEWED AND LEFT AS-IS: Net +2.75 is a deliberate exception, not a gap -- the designer likes a strong-enough Bleeding poison being able to threaten a kill outright, doesn't expect the full stack count to matter much in a real pitched fight (focus-fire kills things before Bleeding's tail value fully realizes, same caveat as every other Bleeding-granting item), and it isn't out of line with Acidic Flask's own similar +2.5 Net under the same curve. No item-text change.

Name: Slowing Poison
Notes: Representative Level 3 (1x Potency, unchanged): 3 stacks Slowed. AP cost and the redundant 'poison-landing' discount both dropped, same as the rest of the batch; persists at full strength across the whole 4-turn window (capped at 4 stacks) rather than decaying, same treatment as the other Poison-delivered curves. Slowed's own base rate doubled this session (a Slowed target needs two movement actions per turn, both hit by the same flat penalty) from 0.55 to 1.1/stack: 1.1 x 3 x 4 x 0.5 = 6.6, not the pre-doubling curve's 3.3. Net moves from -5.7 to -2.4 -- checked across Levels 1-5, holds at a consistent -0.8 to -3.2 through Level 4 before the 4-stack cap starts widening the gap at Level 5 (-6.2). Close enough now that no multiplier change seems warranted -- same call as Vulnerability/Harrying Poison.

Name: Necrotic Poison
Notes: Representative Level 3: 9 stacks Necrotic (three times Potency, bumped from twice -- see below). Necrotic has its own derived value (3/stack when it resolves) rather than generic Debuff, and this poison's decay now follows the generic [Poison] rule (1 stack/hour) like every other flavor, after its own special '2 stacks/hour' carve-out was tidied away this session. Applies a 'does the situation actually come up' discount (x0.75, reflecting that ~1hr/stack persistence gives it plenty of time to actually catch a heal attempt or a Protected grant) and the standard poison-roll discount every Poison in this batch carries (x0.5, reinstated this session after being briefly dropped in error -- this row's own Value was left stale at 13.5/+4.5 through that whole pass and only now catches up): 9 x 3 x 0.75 x 0.5 = 10.125. Unlike Crippled/Vulnerable/Slowed, Necrotic has no stacking cap, so its fit is purely linear -- at the old 2x-Potency grant it read a clean, constant -25% under Target at every Level; bumped to 3x for a tighter (and now slightly over instead of under) constant +12.5% fit, accepted as fine for what's already a fairly niche pick.

Name: Vulnerability Poison
Notes: Bumped 1x->2x Potency (matching Bloody Poison's own precedent), fixing a real shortfall: Crippling Poison's 1x multiplier lands exactly on Target because Crippled's own per-stack rate (1.5) is high enough at that multiplier, but Vulnerable's rate (1) can't reach Target the same way at 1x -- not a poison-specific issue, just a lower-rate keyword needing a bigger multiplier to match. Representative Level 3 (Potency 3, so 6 stacks): full-strength-across-the-2-turn-window formula 1 x 6 x 2 = 12, Net = 12-9 = 3. An accepted overshoot, same magnitude as Bloody Poison's own +2.75 -- per the designer, Poisons can reasonably carry a wider balance berth than other items (single-target, and a dedicated alchemist gets more value from steady low-Level use than from maxing out Potency for one huge application), so the top end running a bit hot isn't the primary concern.

Name: Harrying Poison
Notes: Bumped 1x->2x Potency, same fix and same reasoning as Vulnerability Poison above -- Harrying Poison already reuses Vulnerable's exact formula (continuously-active penalty against incoming threats for the ~1hr/stack survival window, not Harried's normal one-shot-per-turn shape), so it needed the same multiplier bump for the same reason. Representative Level 3 (6 stacks): 1 x 6 x 2 = 12, Net = 12-9 = 3. Same accepted-overshoot call as Vulnerability Poison.

Name: Psychosis Poison
Notes: Bumped 1x->2x Potency, same fix as Vulnerability/Harrying Poison. Representative Level 3 (6 stacks): 6 x 2.2 (Frightened's own rate) x 0.75 (future-hit-lands discount, loosened from 0.5 to reflect the ~1hr persistence window) = 9.9, Net = 9.9-9 = 0.9 -- a genuinely clean fit, the best-landing of the three bumped this pass.

Name: Travel Rations
Notes: Pure logistics item (a day's food, never spoils) -- grants no combat-facing mechanic at all. Out of scope for this Value model; left at Value 0 / Net = -Target rather than force a meaningless number. Not a balance concern, just not what this model prices.

Name: Power Snack
Notes: Sift 6 cards (Level x6), using the corrected Sift weight (~0.60/card -- see design/balance_weights_notes.md; simulated value captured within ~18 draws/day, derived from Baseline's own attack-frequency numbers, not the old sheet's unexplained 0.64). Rate and Target both scoped to 'per day' consistently (Rate=1, Target=Level x 4 for a once-daily item, per the corrected once-per-day convention). No weight used here changed further this pass -- unchanged from the prior recompute.

Name: Hearty Meal
Notes: Heals an extra 1 Shallow Health (Level) on the next full night's rest, guaranteed. Rate=1/Target=Level x 4 (once-per-day convention). Lands exactly at Net 0, the cleanest result in the whole Food batch. No weight used here changed this pass -- unchanged.

Name: Muscular Feast
Grants: Bleeding:2(prevented) or Crippled:2(prevented) or Slowed:2(prevented), AP:0
Notes: Prevents the next 2 stacks (twice Level) of Bleeding/Crippled/Slowed before the next rest. Recomputed with the prevention-contingency discount removed per the designer's call (see balance.md). Bleeding(2)=8, Crippled(2)=4.5, Slowed(2)=3.3, averaged across the three since which one triggers isn't the player's choice: 5.267, no AP cost (Food item). Net +1.267 -- a modest overshoot past the Level-1 threshold (0.8), accepted as-is per the designer.

Name: Soul Soup

Name: Armor of Constitutional Integrity
Notes: Cut its Neck-slot duplicate, Periapt of Constitutional Integrity (I175) -- word-for-word identical text, and a clear mismatch for Neck's own design lane ('niche, boring, passive utility, deliberately not defensive' per RULES_DESIGN.md's slot philosophy) -- almost certainly a pre-slot-philosophy leftover never reconciled once Torso became the defense-designated slot. Widened this item's own trigger from Poison-only to 'Poison, Disease, or similar bodily threat' to match Resilience's own stated domain ('resisting the adverse effects of poison, disease, exhaustion...'), raising how often it's actually relevant. Per the designer: Poison alone comes up roughly 1 in 2-3 fights (used 0.4), hitting ~2 instances per player when it does; widening the trigger category bumps that to an estimated 0.5. BadLuck: 0.5 x 2 x 2.2 = 2.2. GoodLuck(Resilience, permanent, ~1 flip/encounter assumed) = 2.4. Total = 4.6, Net = 4.6-6 = -1.4 -- a real improvement from the pure-Poison version's -1.84 (which was itself already better than the original -3.05 before the frequency was refined), and close enough to accept under the same Masterwork-berth allowance as the Torso Resist items.

Name: Lifeforce Plate (L3)
Notes: At the end of the wearer's turn, refill to 1 stack of Protected if at 0. Priced against the broader "~2.5 relevant empty moments/encounter" read of that trigger (not the stricter 1.875-hits anchor used elsewhere for a guaranteed major hit) -- Lifeforce Plate's trigger also catches incidental chip damage, not just the big swing, so the wider count is the better fit. Considered and rejected: pricing as "assume every one of the 1.875 hits/player/encounter lands while this item's Protected is up," which collapses back to treating the raw hit-count itself as the refill frequency with no discount -- mathematically reproduces the original, stricter estimate almost exactly (Net -3.375 here) rather than giving a new, better-justified number, so it was set aside in favor of the broader empty-moments read. Value = 2.5 x Protected(1)=3 = 7.5, Net = 7.5-9 = -1.5. Accepted below Target as part of the Masterwork single-slot-scarcity allowance, same as the rest of this Torso cluster.

Name: Lifeforce Plate (L5)
Notes: Level-5 clause tops the wearer back up to 2 stacks whenever below that, so both the base refill and the bonus stack are assumed to fire together at the same ~2.5/encounter rate. Value = 2.5 x Protected(2)=6 = 15, Net = 15-15 = 0, an exact fit at the Level-5 threshold -- see the L3 row's note for the full derivation and the rejected stricter alternative.

Name: Coat of Knit Flesh (L2)
Notes: Revised: prevented stacks are priced at Bleeding's full linear rate (4/stack, uncapped), not the tapered value(n) curve -- that curve's asymptotic cap models the chance an *enemy* target dies or the fight ends before every stack finishes decaying, which doesn't apply the same way to a player wearing this, who persists through the whole encounter/day and genuinely eats every stack's Health cost eventually (see the Bleeding correction note above). Bumped from preventing 1 to 2 stacks/day to land exactly on Target: Value = 2 x 4 = 8, Net = 8-8 = 0. Also prompted the general glossary reword ("Each stack of this that decays at the end of your turn deals 1 Health loss") tying the Health cost explicitly to natural decay, not to removal by any means.

Name: Coat of Knit Flesh (L4)
Notes: Same full-linear-rate correction as the L2 row -- see its note. Bumped from 2 to 4 stacks/day to land exactly on Target: Value = 4 x 4 = 16, Net = 16-16 = 0.

Name: Dauntless Wrap (L1)
Notes: [Thrice the enhancement's Level] stacks of Protected, granted the first time each day the wearer would be Downed, before that Health loss lands. Flat once/day Protected-stack pricing (stacks x 3) wildly overshot Target (+5 to +25 across Levels) -- that rate assumes stacks realized gradually across a normal fight, not a single guaranteed lump delivered at the one moment it's certain to matter. Discounted instead by realized trigger frequency: not every day produces a hit that would Down the wearer at all, and even then it has to land on this specific character rather than another party member -- landed on roughly once every 3 adventuring days (comparable rarity to the established Poison-frequency convention, scaled to a per-day cadence), folding in the designer's own point that a fight bad enough to threaten a Down is already a losing one, so this only ever helps when things are going poorly. Rescoped per the once/day convention (Target = Level x 4).

Name: Fitted Armor
Notes: Reworked from '-1 Might Requirement' (no documented mechanical consequence exists anywhere in rulebook.md for failing a Might Requirement, so the old text was unpriceable) into a flat +1 Physical Resist grant -- the Physical-damage sibling of Elemental-Resistant Armor, except Physical doesn't need a chosen-element pick since it's always relevant. Priced against the assumption that only a tank/bruiser playstyle picks this up (per the designer: the item should be balanced for who actually buys it, not an average character) -- takes 50% more attacks than the party-average baseline, so Physical Resist's own rate scales with the hit-count term: 5.0 x 1.5 = 7.5/point. Value = 1 x 7.5 = 7.5. Landed on Level 2 (Target 6, Net +1.5) over Level 3 (Net -1.5) since this grant carries no risk or guesswork the way Elemental-Resistant Armor's chosen-element bet does -- a tank gets full, guaranteed value every fight, so it doesn't need the same below-Target discount used elsewhere in this cluster for a riskier pick; the built-in self-selection (only the right build wants it) already does the limiting work instead.

Name: Fortified Armor
Grants: Resist:1(conditional, Extra Success trigger, tank assumption 1.5x hits)
Notes: Reworded from 'a red card was flipped' -- a stale reference to an older design where Hearts/Diamonds paired with bonus successes. Current rules tie Extra Successes (and their +1 damage) to matching the attacking Skill's own single governing suit, not a fixed red/black split (rulebook.md), so the accurate current-rules trigger is 'the attack scored an Extra Success' -- this also fixes the item to actually do what it was designed for: soften spikes specifically on the hits that already dealt bonus damage, not an arbitrary half the deck. Priced at the honest suit-match rate (25%, the established suit-scaling convention) x Physical Resist's rate (5.0) x tank assumption (1.5x hits, per the designer -- this is a consistent-protection item for a tank dealing with many attacks): Value = 0.25 x 5.0 x 1.5 = 1.875, Net = 1.875-9 = -7.125, the deepest Net in this cluster. Accepted deliberately, not as a miss: per the designer, this is meant to have a higher ceiling than a flat expected-value model can price, since it's specifically countering burst/spike damage (a real, separately-flagged blind spot in the Resist model -- see balance_weights_notes.md) rather than shaving average damage, and there's real design headroom to expand which enemies can score Extra Successes (e.g. Good Luck to hit) going forward. Preferred leaving this underpowered by the flat model over inflating it to hit a Net the model can't actually justify.

Name: Sash of Deep Pockets
Notes: First Storage-archetype items priced this pass -- checked rulebook.md's Retrieving Items rule first: a belt pouch is already an 'easy' 1-AP location with no stated mundane capacity limit, so these items aren't saving AP over a normal belt, they're converting a soft GM-adjudicated 'sure, you can fit that' into a hard guarantee. Priced capacity as the AP saved (1 AP, 2.75) on a realistic 'genuinely extra slots used' ceiling of 3 (a character rarely wants more than a handful of consumables in easy reach beyond what a normal belt already plausibly holds), realized at the niche/rare trigger frequency (1/3, from balance_weights.csv's Situational Multipliers) -- a capacity crunch big enough to matter isn't everyday. Rescoped to the once/day convention (Target = Level x4). Capacity: 3 x 2.75 x 1/3 = 2.75. Sash of Deep Pockets' pouches also fit 1-meter objects (not just small Potion/Grenade-sized ones), a real qualitative difference from the other two Storage items -- credited 1 more genuinely-useful large-object slot at the same rate: 1 x 2.75 x 1/3 = 0.917. Total Value = 2.75+0.917 = 3.667, Net = 3.667-8 = -4.33. Assumes optimal use throughout (the owner actually carries useful items in these slots), matching the 'rational player' convention used elsewhere in this model.

Name: Placeholder's Bottomless Belt
Notes: Same Storage-capacity model as Sash of Deep Pockets (see its note for the full derivation) -- small-object pouches only, no large-object or secrecy component. 20 nominal pouches doesn't translate to 20x value; it caps at the same realistic 3-genuinely-extra-slots ceiling as Sash and Smuggler's Belt, since a character rarely wants more consumables in easy reach than that regardless of how many pouches exist. Value = 3 x 2.75 x 1/3 = 2.75, Net = 2.75-4 = -1.25 (Level 1, once/day Target = 4). The lower Level (1, vs the other two's 2) is doing the real differentiating work here, not the pouch count.

Name: Smuggler's Belt
Notes: Same Storage-capacity model (2.75, see Sash of Deep Pockets' note) plus a secrecy component: the 'automatically fails to discover' guarantee modeled as Good Luck-tier (2.4, a near-certain success, not just a modest edge) on a Stealth-adjacent concealment check, at the same niche/rare frequency (1/3 -- most days nobody's frisking you). Secrecy: 2.4 x 1/3 = 0.8. Total Value = 2.75+0.8 = 3.55, Net = 3.55-8 = -4.45 (Level 2, once/day Target = 8). Assumes optimal use (the owner actually has contraband worth hiding when it matters), matching the 'rational player' convention used elsewhere.

Name: Mendicant's Cord
Notes: As a Move, shift up to 2 points from one Defense to another (self or a willing adjacent creature) -- priced at Acc/Def's flat rate (1/point, Locked): 2 points = Value 2. Per the designer's 'assume optimal use' steer, the lowered Defense is assumed to never actually get tested (that's the whole point of moving points away from it), so only the +2 gain is credited, not also discounted for the -2 elsewhere. Real judgment call, flagged rather than silently decided: did NOT subtract the 1 AP cost (2.75) the way a Grenade/Potion's AP gets charged as a negative grant -- this isn't substituting for an attack the way those are (no Autoswing-style opportunity cost applies), and it matches the 0-AP precedent already used for the Ring Masterwork items' reactive/utility triggers. If that read is wrong and AP should be charged, Net drops to roughly -4.75 (Value 2-2.75=-0.75) instead. Rate=1 (once/encounter -- a single well-timed read of the fight's real threat, not a repeated action). Net = 2-6 = -4 (Level 2, Target 6).
